file_headers.note: No file states a vertical CRS, so the datum rests on documentation, not the data.

checks.file: ESA tile Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_N18_00_W067_00_DEM.tif (s3://copernicus-dem-30m, read by HTTP range)

geoid_offset.method: Every 10th row and column of the 1 arc-second grid, SRTM land samples only (SRTMGL1N > 10), 98,862 samples. N(EGM2008) - N(EGM96) from PROJ 9.8.1 (pyproj 3.8.0) grids us_nga_egm08_25.tif and us_nga_egm96_15.tif (cdn.proj.org), as the EGM96 height of a point at EGM2008 height 0. COP30 on EGM96 = COP30 + that difference.
geoid_offset.transformation: Inverse of WGS 84 to EGM2008 height (1) + WGS 84 to EGM96 height (1) (with axis order normalized for visualization)

interpretation: Over Puerto Rico the EGM2008 and EGM96 geoids differ by -0.95 to +1.09 m (mean +0.31 m). Re-expressing COP30 on EGM96 raises the COP30 - SRTMGL1 median from 1.14 m to 1.38 m and leaves the spread unchanged, so the datum difference does not explain COP30 standing higher than SRTM; surface, epoch and processing differences do.
